children: The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 1330 GMT on Monday:
** German drugmaker Merck KGaA
said  it will acquire Silence Therapeutics
in an all-cash deal for about $1.3 billion, adding precision engineered medicines and gene silencing to its portfolio.
** US consumer goods packaging maker Silgan Holdings
and private equity firm American Industrial Partners will acquire Trivium Packaging in a deal that would value the European firm at $3.4 billion, including debt, the companies said.
** US investment firm KKR
said it will sell railcar-leasing company Infinity Transportation to peer Ares Management
for about $2.9 billion.
** Australian coal miner New Hope
said it would acquire unlisted peer Malabar Resources in a deal valued at about A$2.4 billion ($1.67 billion), giving it full ownership of the Maxwell coal mine in New South Wales.
** Australia's FleetPartners

said it had entered binding agreement to be bought by Pacific Equity Partners-backed SG Fleet in a deal valuing the vehicle leasing firm at A$1.13 billion ($786.71 million), sending its shares to a record high.
** Austrian engine and engine parts manufacturer Steyr Motors
said US drone maker Red Cat Holdings
plans to acquire the company in a deal valued at about €204.8 million ($230 million).
** French supermarket chain Carrefour
has entered into an agreement with Colruyt Group
to acquire local food retail company Codifrance for €152 million ($171 million), it said.
** German defence group Rheinmetall
and Swiss-based shipping company MSC have acquired Romanian shipyard Mangalia for €138 million ($155 million) and aim to develop it for both civilian and military shipbuilding, Rheinmetall said.
